decision: Keep Item.schedule authoritative and keep occurrence execution state separate from schedule definition.

ownership.creatorChange: A new canonical content version; it never mutates a user's past run.
ownership.executionState: ExecutionRun item state keyed by itemId and occurrenceKey.
ownership.stepGroupingHint: Display/grouping context only; never authoritative schedule.
ownership.projectionResolvedDate: Derived at projection time; not source evidence.

effectiveSchedulePrecedence: UserFlowCopy Item scheduleOverride, including explicit null
unsaved UI buffer, not persisted until saved

allowedEvidence: user has not added a date
scheduleModes.notes: Lesson order, Step title, source order, age index, or sequence number alone does not create a date.

forbidden: test fixture date written back as source fact

allowedEvidence: source-defined eligibility, application, renewal, or visit window
scheduleModes.projectionRule: Retain the full window in description/data and generate at most one declared reminder occurrence; never one VEVENT per eligible day.

allowedEvidence: source-defined D-day offset plus named user or source anchor
source-defined relative age/date formula plus named anchor
scheduleModes.calendarEligibility: true only after the required anchor value is available
forbidden: inventing an offset from row order
asking the user for a source-owned anchor already captured

sourceOrderMappings.becomesScheduleWhen: The source explicitly binds the sequence to a start anchor, or the user deliberately adds a start anchor as an overlay.
A source or user anchor resolves it to actual dates.
A birth/event anchor and exact source formula exist.

sourceOrderMappings.defaultCanonicalTreatment: Undated Item plus source-explicit condition in conversion-audit sidecar.
sourceOrderMappings.becomesScheduleWhen: The trigger occurred, all operands are known, and a deterministic supported formula resolves the due date.

rules: Recurrence requires an absolute or anchor-offset schedule.
A user-selected cadence is stored in the personal overlay and does not rewrite the source cadence.
Order, challenge length, or a phrase such as 'regularly' is not enough to invent recurrence.
count and until must not conflict; if a destination needs one, the projection policy chooses without changing canonical intent.
Changing future cadence preserves completed past occurrence state.
recurrence.unsupportedSourceRules: Preserve as source detail and require review; do not emit a guessed RRULE.

occurrenceIdentity.icsUidRule: Derive a stable opaque UID from the projection identity tuple and a FlowMe domain; never use title as identity.
invariants: The same Item can have many occurrence states without cloning the canonical Item.
A date edit moves one occurrence through an occurrence override; it does not create a new source Item.
Past occurrence keys and states remain retained after recurrence edits.
A retry or second session at the same local time requires an explicit collision suffix.
Timezone or all-day semantics are part of the occurrence key input.
UID generation is deterministic for the same copy, Item, and occurrence.

serializationDecision.openDetail: The exact escaping/hash encoding and migration behavior for pre-existing exported UIDs must be set during backend implementation.

occurrenceExpansion.rangeRule: Expansion is bounded by the request range, recurrence count/until, or product safety limit; an infinite recurrence is never materialized without a range.
occurrenceExpansion.stateRule: Expansion produces candidate occurrences; ExecutionRun remains the owner of completion, skip, hold, decision, and record state.

sharedScheduleContext.projectionTimeGrouping: Items may share one resolved schedule without sharing completion state.

persistentSharedContextEntity.adoptionRule: Promote only when at least three independent fixtures require cross-Flow shared values that cannot be represented cleanly by Flow setup Fields and bindings.
persistentSharedContextEntity.corpusSidecar: Experimental sharedContextBindings may document repeated values, but are not canonical v1 entities.

allowedSupport: derived from fully traced source/user operands

componentRules: Scheduled Items project to sibling VEVENT components.
VEVENT and VTODO are never nested.
VALARM may be nested in VEVENT or VTODO only when a reminder is explicitly requested.
Flow, Step, and Map are not iCalendar components.

allowedWhen: all children have the same effective schedule
all child Item IDs are included
forbiddenWhen: children have different dates or timezones
the bundle hides a decision or record requirement
the destination would be treated as completion owner

recurrenceExportModes.note: Compact export; destination completion cannot represent FlowMe occurrence state.
Useful for bounded windows; each instance uses the occurrence identity tuple.

validationRules: No Item without an effective schedule may produce VEVENT.
No recurrence may exist without direct source or explicit user provenance.
Every anchor_offset references a declared setup Field.
A source-filled anchor is not requested from the user.
Every date_window has start <= end and its reminder is inside or explicitly before the window.
Every recurring Item state has a non-empty occurrenceKey.
Occurrence identity is unique within one run.
Step bundle projection retains all child Item IDs.
Projection-time resolved dates are not written back as source facts.
VEVENT and VTODO nesting count is zero.
